brief: A display stand with the large platform on a spike where three bases meet.

requirements.requirement: Three bases that meet at one point
requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0, piece:1,-1,0 and piece:1,0,0 meet at one shared corner.

requirements.requirement: A spike standing where the three bases meet
requirements.evidence: The mount spike spike:0#0,0|1,-1|1,0 stands at the corner where (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet.

requirements.requirement: The large platform on that spike
requirements.evidence: The platform-lrg accessory is set on that spike. The parts list shows 'Platform, large' x1.

requirements.requirement: Works as a display stand (something shown on the platform)
requirements.evidence: The large platform gives a raised flat surface for displaying items, but nothing could be shown on it: the configurator refuses props on a spike platform. The props test will fail, since no prop was placed.

finish.summary: Built a three-base display stand. Full hex bases at (0,0), (1,-1) and (1,0) meet at one corner, and a mount spike stands at that corner holding the large platform (spike-acc-platform-lrg, about 52 × 60 mm). As house rules require, the open faces are capped with solid edge caps and the joints are bolted. That makes 17 printed parts plus 12 M6 screws and nuts, about 1099 g of filament. check_build shows no rule issues and the mesh-collision check is clear. I couldn't put an example item on the platform, because the configurator won't place props on a spike platform. So R4 can't be shown here, and its test (one prop) will fail. I chose not to put an item on a base just to pass the test.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
